title: Cascade Cohort Temporal Guardrails and Traffic Policy Engine
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a generalized policy engine that supports cascade cohort rollouts: time-based ramping, cohort sequencing, shadow probing, and SLA-driven auto-rollback. This ticket covers the controller and config surface (traffic split DSL, step schedules, guardrail predicates) and the minimum telemetry hooks needed for safe automation. Goals: 1) declarative config for cohorted releases (cohorts defined by population selectors and time windows), 2) step scheduler that supports fixed-rates, time-delays, and burst windows, 3) guardrail predicates for latency/error/quality and configurable rollback actions, 4) lightweight shadow probing integration to validate variant behavior before exposure, 5) observability contract (per-cohort metrics, SLO evaluation, anomaly signals) for the Console to drive canary recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Config DSL: users can declare cohorts with selectors, initial traffic fraction, step schedule, and rollback predicates in a single policy YAML
Controller: rollout obeys schedule and cohort dependencies and exposes current state via API
Shadow probes: optional shadow traffic path can mirror 1% of relevant traffic to new variant and record deterministic probe metrics
Guardrails: automatic rollback triggers on configured thresholds (p95 latency, error-rate, or quality regression) with configurable cooldown and safety fences
Observability: per-cohort metrics emitted to telemetry pipeline and linked to Console rollouts dashboard
Safety test: run simulated rollout in local simulator that exercises flap/partial-failure and confirms rollback behavior
Docs: PRD + user-facing example policy and migration guide
